# Synthetic protocol fixtures

These files contain explicit synthetic values. They contain no camera recordings or captured biometric data and do not establish device accuracy.

| Files | Origin and purpose |
|---|---|
| `v014_*.bin` | Messages encoded using the original 0.1.4 Python descriptors; protect backward wire compatibility. |
| `swift_phone.bin`, `swift_joystick.bin`, `swift_face_hand.bin`, `blendshape_names.json` | Synthetic messages encoded by the companion app's SwiftProtobuf 1.30 models and canonical blendshape catalog. |
| `swift_stream_hand.bin`, `swift_face_hand_only.bin`, `swift_empty_hand.bin` | Synthetic hand messages emitted through a recording transport by the app's two hand-stream entry points; cover shared decoding and tracking loss. |
| `swift_face_only.bin`, `swift_no_face.bin` | Schema-version-2 face messages; cover independent face output, all 52 coefficients and face loss. |
| `swift_body_*.bin` | Synthetic poses serialized by the app's multi-person codec; cover two people, stable IDs after reordering, missing world registration and empty frames. |
| `hevc_frame.bin`, `hevc_config.json` | A 64 × 64 red test image encoded with libx265, split into length-prefixed NAL data and VPS/SPS/PPS configuration. |

The Swift fixtures are interoperability samples produced by the companion app, not generated by the Python decoder under test. Running the regression suite requires only these checked-in files. Replacing them requires preserving their documented origin and updating the corresponding assertions.
